data.name: Duman
data.gender_notes: Duman is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'd-m-n', meaning 'to remain steadfast, to be firm and unwavering. In Islamic context, it is an attribute of Allah Almighty and is used for individuals who exhibit this quality. The name Duman carries the meaning “Steadfast, resolute” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Duman usually hope their child will grow to embody steadfast, resolute and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing unwavering faith and unyielding commitment to Allah.
data.etymology: Duman belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Steadfast, resolute.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Duman total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Duman" reflects the courage and resilience that are valued in Islamic culture. It evokes images of individuals who have faced hardships and adversity with unwavering determination and perseverance. In the Islamic society, this name would be given to a child as a reminder of the importance of staying strong in times of challenge and to become pillars of strength for their community.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name "Duman" holds great spiritual significance for Muslims. It represents the ideal of remaining steadfast and firm in one's faith, even in the face of temptation, hardship, or adversity. It is a reminder of the importance of staying true to Allah and upholding the Islamic values of patience, perseverance, and unwavering faith. The name "Duman" can be seen as a reminder to strive for inner strength and peace, and to turn to Allah during times of difficulty.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the name of a Berber chief named Duman in his 'Muqaddimah'. He was the prince of the Banu Iznagen in the late 14th century, who controlled the region around Tlemcen in present-day Algeria. Duman is remembered for his military exploits and for his patronage of scholars, including the famous historian Ibn Khaldun himself.
historical_references.context: Berber chief in North Africa, military leader and patron of scholars

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi, in his 'Kitab al-Mawā'iẓ wa-l-ʾIṭḥāraf', describes Duman as a Mamluk amir in Egypt during the early 15th century. He was the governor of Damietta and played a significant role in the defense of Egypt against the Italian crusaders led by Carmagnola.
historical_references.context: Mamluk amir in Egypt, military leader in defense against crusaders
